description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of large language models, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of the proposed “SepLLM” and “StrmLLM” methods, as evaluated in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000 and uses a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with major ticks every 0.1 unit, also on a linear scale. Six distinct lines are plotted: “Vanilla” (purple, solid line) starts at approximately 3.35 and steadily declines to about 2.48; “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid line) begins near 3.35 and decreases to roughly 2.62; “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid line) starts at ~3.35 and ends near 2.52; “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid line) begins at ~3.35 and converges to ~2.50; “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid line) starts at ~3.35 and drops to ~2.49; and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid line) begins at ~3.35 and ends near 2.51. All lines exhibit a steep initial decline in loss followed by a slower, more gradual convergence, with the “Vanilla” model consistently showing the lowest loss across iterations, while “StrmLLM (n=64)” remains the highest among the variants after ~20,000 iterations.
